68-026.r: Gandhi suspended Non-Cooperation (1922) → violent incident at Chauri-Chaura, near Gorakhpur, U.P. (February 1922).

68-030.r: February 2021 → PM Narendra Modi inaugurated Chauri Chaura Centenary Celebration (4 February 2021, Gorakhpur, via video conferencing).

68-031.r: Gandhi called his Satyagraha at Nadiyad (14 April, under martial law after Jallianwala Bagh) his 'Himalayan Blunder'.
68-031.c: Answer not printed (*); question ties it to Non-Cooperation, but explanation names the Nadiyad Satyagraha after Jallianwala Bagh.

68-032.r: Gandhi called for boycott of Prince of Wales' visit (1921) → during Non-Cooperation Movement.

68-033.r: During Chauri-Chaura (4 February 1922) Gandhi was at Bardoli (Gujarat); Bardoli resolution (12 February 1922) withdrew Non-Cooperation, which ended in 1922.

68-035.r: Censure vote against Gandhi for calling off Non-Cooperation, AICC meeting at Delhi, 24 February 1922 → Dr. Moonje.

68-036.r: Chauri Chaura sequence: police firing (4 February 1922) → crowd set police station on fire → Gandhi postponed the movement → Gandhi arrested.

68-037.r: Led Bihar cultivators during Non-Cooperation → Swami Vidyanand, who linked peasant grievances to the movement.

68-038.r: Bihar pleader who left lucrative practice in Non-Cooperation → Rajendra Prasad (author of 'India Divided').

68-039.r: Order: Chauri-Chaura (4 February 1922) → Bardoli Resolutions (12 February 1922) → suspension of Non-Cooperation Movement.

68-040.r: Revival of revolutionary activity in 1923-28 → disappointment at Gandhi's suspension of Non-Cooperation (1922); inspired by Russia, China, Ireland, Turkey.

68-041.r: Non-Cooperation programme (Calcutta and Nagpur, 1920): boycott of law courts and foreign cloth, strict non-violence, panchayats for disputes; titles to be renounced, not retained → three parts.

68-042.r: Rabindranath Tagore wrote that burning foreign clothes in Non-Cooperation was a ruthless (callous) waste; he preferred a constructive programme.

68-044.r: Founded during Non-Cooperation (1920-22): Kashi Vidyapith (1921), Gujarat Vidyapith (1920), Jamia Millia Islamia (Aligarh 1920, later Delhi); BHU earlier (1916, Malviya).

68-046.r: Main outcome of 1921-22 Non-Cooperation, per book → Hindu-Muslim unity; all sections of society joined the national movement.

68-047.r: E.V. Ramasamy 'Periyar' → took part in Non-Cooperation Movement; left Congress in 1925 → both true.

68-048.r: Wrong pair: '1930 - Non-Cooperation'; Non-Cooperation was 1920-1922, 1930 = Civil Disobedience. Correct: 1885 INC, 1905 Bengal Partition, 1909 Morley-Minto.

68-049.r: Correct pair: 1931 - Execution of Rajguru (23 March 1931, with Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev); Lahore Session December 1929; Non-Cooperation 1 August 1920; Rowlatt Satyagraha April 1919.

68-050.r: Gandhi suspended Non-Cooperation in 1922 after Chauri-Chaura (A true); C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru opposed the suspension (R true) → R does not explain A.

68-051.r: Jai Prakash Narayan left Patna College with 20 days left for exams during Non-Cooperation; then joined Congress-run Bihar Vidyapeeth.

68-052.r: Anti-Non-Cooperation Association (1920, Bombay big businessmen) → Jamnadas Dwarkadas, Purshottamdas Thakurdas, Cowasji Jehangir, Pheroze Sethna, M.C. Setalvad.
68-052.c: CGPSC deleted this question. The Association's founders included Jamnadas Dwarkadas and Purshottamdas Thakurdas; option (a) 'Jamna Das Thakur Das' blends their two names.

69-001.r: Swaraj Party formed because → Gandhi withdrew Non-Cooperation, and to enter councils and obstruct the 1919 Act from within; C.R. Das resigned Congress presidency to form it.

69-003.r: Swaraj Party (1923) → C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru, after failure of Non-Cooperation Movement.

69-010.r: Pro-changers (Swarajists) → C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru, Vithalbhai Patel; No-changers → Vallabhbhai Patel, C. Rajagopalachari, Rajendra Prasad (not in Swaraj Party).
69-010.t: Don't confuse Vithalbhai Patel (Swarajist, pro-changer) with Vallabhbhai Patel (no-changer).

69-012.r: Swaraj Dal branch in Bihar → led by Sri Krishna Singh.

69-013.r: Order: Lucknow Pact (1916) → Jallianwala Massacre (1919) → Tilak's death (1920) → Swaraj Party (1923).

69-014.r: Swarajists won 42 of 104 elected seats (November 1923) and joined hands with liberals and independents like Jinnah and Malviya in Central Legislative Assembly.

69-015.r: 'Deshbandhu' (Friend of the Country) → Chittaranjan Das, lawyer who defended Sri Aurobindo Ghosh.
69-015.t: Deshbandhu = C.R. Das; Deenbandhu = Charles Andrews.

69-016.r: 'Swaraj for the masses, not for the classes' → C.R. Das.

69-017.r: Moderates who welcomed Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (Government of India Act 1919), led by Surendranath Banerjee, left Congress → formed (All India) Liberal Federation.

69-018.r: Indian National Liberal Federation (1918) → founded by Surendranath Banerjee after Congress split over Montford Report; T.B. Sapru, V.S. Srinivas Sastri, M.R. Jayakar prominent.

69-019.r: Independent Party (16 December 1922) → Madan Mohan Malviya and Motilal Nehru; Malviya also founded BHU (1916) and Hindu Mahasabha.

69-020.r: First Indian Speaker (President) of Central Legislative Assembly → Vithalbhai Patel, 1925; co-founder of Swaraj Party.

70-001.r: Simon Commission: appointed November 1927 (Baldwin's Conservative Government) to review 1919 Act; visited India 1928; seven members, no Indian → protests.

70-007.r: Simon Commission: Chairman Sir John Simon → Liberal Party; Clement Attlee → Labour Party.

70-008.r: Indians kept out of Simon Commission on Lord Irwin's suggestion → called 'White Commission'; reached India 1928.

70-009.r: Congress boycotted Simon Commission (A) because it had no Indian member (R) → both true, R explains A.

70-010.r: Simon Commission → reviewed working of 1919 Act; headed by Sir John Simon; recommended federal form; opposed by Indian leaders → all true.

70-011.r: Simon Commission recommended replacing dyarchy with responsible government in provinces (1919 Act had provided for a review after 10 years).

70-012.r: Simon Commission visited twice: 3 February to 31 March 1928, and 11 October 1928 to 13 April 1929; so 'second visit 1929-1930' is wrong.

70-013.r: Lala Lajpat Rai injured in lathi charge protesting Simon Commission; Congress Madras session (December 1927) decided boycott; slogan 'Simon Go Back'.

70-015.r: Lala Lajpat Rai led protest at Lahore (1928) against Simon Commission (reached Bombay 3 February 1928) as it had no Indian member → both true, R explains A.

70-016.r: Nehru Report (1928), reply to Simon Commission, demanded Dominion Status → All-Party Committee chaired by Motilal Nehru; Jawaharlal Nehru secretary; 10 members incl. two Muslims.

70-017.r: Dominion Status: Motilal Nehru asked (March 1926) for a constitution conference, but option pairs him with G.B. Pant; book picks Tej Bahadur Sapru and Jaykar.
70-017.c: Shaky key: explanation credits Motilal Nehru with the demand and rejects (b) only because Pant is paired with him.

70-018.r: Nehru Report (1928) → Dominion Status, not Complete Independence; joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities; Fundamental Rights → 2 and 3 correct.

70-019.r: Independence for India League (1928) → Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhash Chandra Bose, demanding complete Independence over Dominion Status.

70-020.r: Nehru Report → drafted by committee headed by Motilal Nehru; subject: constitutional arrangements in India.

70-021.r: Jinnah's 14 Points → March 1929, in protest against Nehru Report, to safeguard Muslims' political rights.

70-022.r: Independence for India League (Jawaharlal Nehru, Subhash Bose) → founded in opposition to Nehru Report; demanded complete Independence as immediate goal.

70-023.r: All Parties Conference (Delhi, February 1928) → President Dr. M.A. Ansari; 29 organisations; reply to Simon Commission and Lord Birkenhead's challenge.

71-001.r: Hasrat Mohani → proposed Swaraj = Complete Independence free from all foreign control (Ahmedabad Session 1921; Hakim Ajmal Khan acting President as C.R. Das was in jail).

71-003.r: Congress first passed Complete Independence (Purna Swaraj) resolution → Lahore Session, December 1929, President Jawaharlal Nehru; followed Calcutta 1928 ultimatum on Nehru Report.

71-006.r: Before 1947, 26 January = Purna Swaraj Day; Lahore 1929 resolution; Nehru hoisted flag on Ravi bank 31 December 1929; first observed 26 January 1930.

71-014.r: Jawaharlal Nehru first presided over Congress → Lahore Session 1929 (Complete Independence passed; 26 January to be 'Purna Swadhinta Divas').
